answer: Hardware attestation makes identity unclonable: an agent economy can require every key to be minted inside a secure enclave whose attestation signal is burned into the silicon - one chip, one identity, ever. Software cannot copy the copper lattice anchoring that signal, so a sybil operator cannot fork identities in a rented datacenter; each fake key demands a physical device it must buy, ship, and power. A gale of registrations becomes a gale of real hardware purchases, and stocking thousands of enrolled machines costs far more than any reward the fleet could ever harvest.
